$comment: ores-locks-and-leases — JSON Schema authority. Independent peer of contracts/typespec/main.tsp (ORESoftware/ores-contracts): neither is generated from the other; `npx ores-contracts check` must find them equivalent.

LockKey.description: A caller-chosen lock identity. Convention: `<org>/<domain>/<name>`, e.g. `zed-pkg/registry/publish:zed-lib-core`.

AdvisoryKey.description: The Postgres advisory-lock integer derived from a LockKey: FNV-1a 64 over the UTF-8 bytes, reinterpreted as a two's-complement bigint. Vectors: conformance/cases/advisory-key.json.

FencingToken.description: A monotonically increasing token minted by the lease authority on every grant. Writes guarded by the lease carry it so a stale holder cannot clobber a newer one.

FencingTokenText.description: Lossless wire and storage form of a Fiducia uint64 token: canonical unsigned decimal text with no sign, whitespace, fractional part, or leading zeroes. Implementations also reject values above 18446744073709551615.

FenceDecisionKind.description: Outcome of comparing an incoming fencing token and idempotency identity with a stored watermark.

FencedWriteRequest.description: One application mutation guarded by a Fiducia fencing token.

payloadSha256.description: Lowercase SHA-256 of the canonical mutation payload.

FenceWatermark.description: The last accepted write for one `(tenantScope, resourceKey)` identity.

FenceDecision.description: Pure fencing decision. `shouldApply` is true only for `advanced`.

currentToken.description: Token that remains current after the decision.

previousToken.description: Watermark before the decision; absent only for the first accepted write.

LockLayers.description: Which coordination layers a routine engages. Both false is a deliberate pass-through (tests, single-writer dev).

fiducia.description: Engage the fiducia-cloud lease (outermost layer, cross-host, TTL-bounded, fenced).

pgAdvisory.description: Engage a Postgres advisory lock (inner layer, single-database, released with the transaction or session).

PgScope.description: How the Postgres advisory lock is scoped. transaction: pg_advisory_xact_lock inside a transaction the routine opens; released at commit/rollback; the caller's work runs inside it. session: pg_advisory_lock / pg_advisory_unlock on one dedicated connection; no transaction is opened.

LockStep.description: One observable action in a lock routine. Maintained transactions may emit fiducia.renew dynamically without changing the legacy static lock-plan matrix.

LockPlan.description: A pure function of the inputs; every implementation must produce the same steps. Dynamic maintenance renewals are intentionally not included.

wait.description: true: block up to the wait budget; false: fail fast with `contention` when any layer is held.

AcquireOptions.description: Acquisition tuning shared by every layer.

ttlMs.description: Lease TTL in milliseconds for the fiducia layer. The lease lapses if never renewed or released.

waitTimeoutMs.description: Time to poll the fiducia authority before giving up, in milliseconds. Maintained PostgreSQL waits use this as their bounded advisory-lock budget; ignored when wait is false.

retryIntervalMs.description: Poll interval while waiting on the fiducia or maintained PostgreSQL advisory-lock layer, in milliseconds.

holder.description: Caller identity for the fiducia layer; also the release key. Absent: an unguessable generated id.

LeaseMaintenanceOptions.description: Renewal cadence for a maintained Fiducia + PostgreSQL transaction. Runtimes reject non-positive values and values greater than half the acquisition TTL before acquiring either layer.

LeaseGrant.description: A held fiducia grant, as returned by the lease authority.

leaseExpiresMs.description: Absolute expiry in Unix milliseconds when the authority reports it.

LockErrorKind.description: Why an acquisition or guarded run failed. contention: a layer is held by someone else and wait was false. timeout: the wait budget elapsed. lost_lease: the fiducia lease could not be renewed or was reaped — fenced authority is lost and the guarded work must not continue. transport: transport/HTTP failure talking to the lease authority; ownership is unknown. database: the database refused the advisory-lock statement, the transaction, or the connection. work: the caller's work returned an error; outer layers were still released/rolled back. invalid_plan: the inputs cannot be planned, including an unsafe renewal cadence.

LockError.description: The structured failure every implementation surfaces.
